definition: To swallow semen; the act of ingesting ejaculate during or after fellatio.
notes: Compound of 吞 (swallow) + 精 (semen/vital essence); 精 has a classical flavor that makes the term feel simultaneously crude and slightly euphemistic; no equivalent single English word exists — 'swallowing' requires context to carry the sexual meaning.

definition: Sexual desire; the psychological and physiological drive toward sexual activity.
notes: The standard clinical and everyday term for libido in Mandarin; carries no inherent negative connotation; used in medical literature, sex education, and casual speech with equal ease.

definition: Carnal or erotic desire that fuses emotional longing with physical lust; romantic-sexual passion.
notes: 情 (emotion/love) + 欲 (desire); carries more literary and emotionally freighted connotations than 性欲; common in fiction, poetry, and classical erotica; implies desire that is simultaneously sensual and sentimental, whereas 性欲 is purely physiological.

definition: Desire or longing in a general sense; in sexual contexts, appetite or craving for sexual experience.
notes: Broad term covering any strong desire (wealth, power, sex); sexual meaning depends entirely on context; less clinical than 性欲 and less emotionally specific than 情欲; mapping to 'lust' is approximate — the term is neutral and wide-spectrum.

definition: Lewd, licentious, or sexually dissolute; classically also means excessive or immoderate in any domain.
notes: A classical character with over two thousand years of moral-condemnatory use; rarely appears alone in modern speech — primarily functions as a prefix in compounds (淫秽 obscene, 淫荡 lascivious, 奸淫 rape); the government censorship term for pornography (淫秽) uses this character, cementing its legal-moral register.

definition: Lascivious, wanton, or sexually dissolute; describes a person or behavior as shamelessly and excessively sexual.
notes: 淫 (lewd) + 荡 (dissolute/wanton); stronger and cruder than 淫 alone; carries strong pejorative charge, most often applied to women to stigmatize open sexuality; can describe behavior, expression, or atmosphere as well as character.

definition: Sexually loose, slutty, or provocatively arousing; applied to a person (usually a woman) it implies shameless sexual openness; used admiringly in internet slang for someone exuding raw sexual energy.
notes: Originally meant 'smelly' or 'disturbing'; sexual meaning may derive from association with the smell of arousal; highly ambivalent — can be a stinging insult or a sex-positive compliment depending on register; forms productive compounds: 骚货 (slut), 骚劲 (slutty energy), 撩骚 (to flirt crudely); partially reclaimed in youth and queer internet spaces.

definition: Lustful, erotic, or pornographic; as a standalone adjective or productive suffix, marks content or behavior as sexual or sexually titillating.
notes: Primary meaning is 'color'; the sexual meaning derives from Buddhist usage — 色 as sensory illusion and carnal attachment; ubiquitous as a sexual prefix or suffix: 色情 (pornography), 好色 (lecherous), 色鬼 (pervert), 色狼 (sexual predator), 色眯眯 (lecherous-looking); mild in isolation but marks sexual valence across a vast lexical network.

definition: Lecherous; fond of sex; describes a person as excessively preoccupied with sexual desire or the pursuit of sexual partners.
notes: Literally 'fond of color/sex'; a classical compound attested since antiquity in texts like the Analects ('I have never met a man as fond of virtue as he is of female beauty'); today mildly pejorative but often used self-deprecatingly or humorously; less harsh than 色鬼; predominantly applied to men.

definition: Pornographic; pornography; sexually explicit material designed to arouse; the standard modern Chinese term for pornographic content.
notes: Used adjectivally and nominally (色情内容 pornographic content, 色情网站 porn website); the formal government censorship term is 淫秽色情; this compound spans journalism, law, casual speech, and platform content moderation equally; effectively a 1:1 equivalent of English 'pornography' in all registers.

definition: A pervert or sex maniac; a person obsessively or shamelessly dominated by lust.
notes: Literally 'sex ghost/demon'; 鬼 is a productive Mandarin insult suffix (酒鬼 drunk, 懒鬼 lazybones, 赌鬼 compulsive gambler) implying the person is possessed by a force; severity sits between English 'horndog' and 'sex offender' — crude mockery rather than criminal accusation; almost always applied to men.

definition: To be in heat; to experience intense, uncontrolled sexual arousal — applied to humans as a crude metaphor for animalistic lust.
notes: The biologically standard term for animal estrus; when applied to humans it is deliberately dehumanizing, implying the subject has lost rational control to animal sexual drives; used as an insult, as a humorous self-deprecating admission of arousal, and in internet meme contexts; its technical zoological origin gives it a strange dual clinical/crude quality.

definition: The fire of desire; an intense, burning sexual craving described metaphorically as an internal flame consuming the body.
notes: 欲 (desire) + 火 (fire); most commonly appears in the set phrase 欲火中烧 ('desire-fire burning inside'), a fixed idiom for being consumed by lust; widespread in romance novels and classical erotica; elevated literary register, not used in casual speech; the fire metaphor implies both irresistibility and suffering.

definition: Amorous feelings; the stirring of romantic or sexual desire in the heart, associated with the vitality and awakening of spring.
notes: 春 (spring) has been a classical Chinese euphemism for sexuality and romance since at least the Tang dynasty; 春心 appears in Tang poetry and classical drama; implies tender, nascent desire rather than raw lust; compare 春意 which describes atmospheric mood rather than internal feeling.

definition: An amorous or sensually charged mood or atmosphere; the feeling of romantic and sexual longing evoked by the warmth and fecundity of spring.
notes: More atmospheric and external than 春心 (an inner feeling); 春意 describes a quality in a space or scene; 春意盎然 means suffused with springtime/erotic energy; frequently used in double-entendre contexts to imply a sexually charged atmosphere without naming it directly; the less personal framing makes it slightly more literary and slightly more common in euphemistic contexts.

definition: Frigidity; low or absent sexual desire; describes a person as sexually unresponsive or indifferent to sex.
notes: Literally 'sexually cold-bland'; used both clinically and colloquially; unlike English 'frigid' (which skews female and pejorative), 性冷淡 is applied to men and women with approximately equal frequency in modern Chinese usage; also famously co-opted as an internet aesthetic describing cold minimalist interior design, creating frequent humorous collision between the two meanings in youth culture.

definition: To flirt with someone; to tease or provoke romantic or sexual interest through playful, suggestive words or behavior.
notes: Exploded in Chinese internet slang circa 2014–2016; the character originally meant 'to lift' or 'to stir up'; the sexual/flirtatious meaning implies deliberate playful provocation — lighter than seduction, heavier than friendly attention; spawned derivatives 撩骚 (crude flirting), 撩妹 (flirt with women), 撩汉 (flirt with men); one of the defining internet-era Mandarin slang terms; 'to flirt' is only an approximate gloss because 撩 implies more intentional teasing than passive charm.

definition: To flirt provocatively or make sexually charged advances; to tease someone with crude or raw sexual suggestiveness.
notes: Combines 撩 (flirt/tease) and 骚 (slutty/provocative); cruder than 撩 alone by a significant margin; implies the flirting has a raw, sexually explicit or animalistic edge rather than cute playfulness; can be used critically (he was making crude advances on her) or admiringly in sex-positive contexts; less common than 撩 and skews toward describing behavior rather than as a self-descriptor.

definition: An aphrodisiac; any substance believed to stimulate or intensify sexual desire.
notes: Literally 'spring medicine/drug'; 春 is the classical euphemism for sexuality; also called 媚药 (charm drug) in some contexts; covers traditional herbal remedies, chemical substances, and folk remedies equally; frequently appears in news coverage of date rape drug cases, where 春药 is often conflated with rohypnol in popular and media usage.

definition: Charming, alluring, or seductively attractive; a quality of feminine beauty and manner that captivates and draws sexual or romantic desire.
notes: Classical character with strong feminine connotations; used in compounds: 妩媚 (charming/coquettish), 媚眼 (come-hither eyes), 魅媚 (enchanting allure); rarely standalone in modern speech but highly productive in literary, cosmetic, and advertising registers; implies an active and somewhat deliberate seductive quality — the subject radiates attraction rather than merely possessing it passively.

definition: Seductively cunning like a fox spirit; describes a woman who bewitches and manipulates men through sexual allure and guile, implying she morally corrupts her targets.
notes: Derived from the Chinese fox spirit (狐狸精 húlíjīng) mythology, in which female fox demons assume human form to seduce men and drain their life force; 狐媚 is always pejorative — the subject is beautiful and sexually captivating but dangerous and corrupting; the closest English concepts are 'vamp' or 'femme fatale' but neither captures the specific folkloric frame of demonic seduction; 'vixen' is the closest single English word but lacks the supernatural connotation.

definition: A slutty or sexually provocative manner or energy; the quality of exuding raw, shameless sexual forwardness as a characteristic disposition.
notes: 骚 (slutty/provocative) + 劲 (energy/manner/spirit); describes a quality of behavior rather than a fixed identity label; can be critical or, increasingly in sex-positive internet slang, admiring; analogous to the English internet coinage 'slut energy' or, structurally, 'big dick energy' as a vibe descriptor; more behavioral and momentary than 骚货 (a stable identity insult).

definition: Hormone; used colloquially to explain or humorously attribute sexual attraction and arousal to uncontrollable physiological forces.
notes: Phonetic loanword from English 'hormone'; in everyday sexual usage (荷尔蒙飙升 'hormones surging', 荷尔蒙满满 'full of hormones') it functions as a light-hearted or self-deprecating biologizing of sexual attraction, roughly equivalent to English 'my hormones are raging'; the mapping to sexual_arousal is approximate — the term is the mechanism, not the state, but usage conflates them.

definition: Temptation, seduction, or enticement; the act or quality of attracting someone toward sensual or sexual indulgence.
notes: General-purpose term for temptation of any kind — food, money, power, sex; sexual meaning is context-dependent; slightly more morally charged than 性感 (sexy) because it frames attraction as an active luring force on the target's will; used in religious moral discourse (抵抗诱惑 'resist temptation') and everyday flirtation contexts with the same word; mapping to eroticism is approximate — 诱惑 emphasizes the effect on the tempted rather than the quality of the stimulus.

definition: Sexy; sexually attractive; possessing a quality of physical or behavioral allure that evokes sexual desire in others.
notes: The standard modern Mandarin term for 'sexy'; used without stigma in advertising, entertainment media, and casual speech; applies freely to persons, clothing, voices, and other attributes; entered Mandarin via Japanese セクシー as a calque of English 'sexy'; nearly a 1:1 functional equivalent of English 'sexy' across all usage contexts and registers.
